growth.name: Growth
growth.method: Growing companies that already make money. Gates: quarterly revenue YoY ≥ 20%, TTM net income > 0, prior-year quarterly revenue ≥ $50M, ROE present. Rank: profitability - the average of five percentile ranks inside the list: return on equity, return on assets, operating income / assets, cash flow / assets and gross profit / assets (at least two needed). Score is the percentile of that average. Revenue growth is a gate, not a score. Six-month return versus QQQ is shown beside the rank; it is the tape, not the score. Every name that passes the gates is published; Growth is not cut to a top-10% shortlist.

undervalued.name: Cheap on operating profit
undervalued.method: Cheap on operating profit: TTM operating income / EV, where EV is equity market cap plus interest-bearing debt minus cash. Requires positive operating income, a consistent statement, net margin between -20% and 80% when reported, and cash plus debt on the same filing asset date; long-term debt with no current-debt line counts no debt due within a year. Names without EV are out. The published list is the top 10% of that set, at most 150 names. OI / equity cap is shown beside the rank so leverage is visible; it is not the score. Leases and NCI are not in EV. Generic OI / EV excludes banks, insurers, diversified financials, mortgage companies, and REITs because operating income and debt do not have the same economic meaning in those sectors. Insurers are also found by SEC industry code 63xx, since the listing calls managed care Medical Specialities.

composite.name: Overlap · two or more lists
composite.method: Names that appear on at least two of the published Strength, Growth and Undervalued lists. Strength and Undervalued contribute only their shortlists (top 10%, at most 150). Growth contributes every gated name. Every member is scored on the same scale: the average of three market-wide percentiles - Strength score, profitability (Growth's ranking measure: the average of five percentile ranks - ROE, ROA, operating income, cash flow and gross profit to assets) and operating income / EV - whichever lists it joined. A percentile that cannot be computed (a financial company, missing EV, fewer than two profitability measures) counts as a neutral 50; non-positive operating income scores 0 on OI / EV. A company with negative shareholders' equity (liabilities larger than assets) is not eligible, as in Fama-French's profitability factor and S&P's top quality indices. The first 10 ranks hold at most 3 companies per sector; companies held back keep their score and follow. The sector limit is a diversification rule, not a forecast.
